summary: loader-diag-xnu-sb-md1 (the documented Stage A re-run) ran once on the S24 (decision 0036, RECOVERY only, restored from the pinned stock, Android checked). The pre-registered analysers, run unchanged, give chain row 9 and Stage A row A8 (not evaluated): the kernel text of the run sits in the collector's second boot and the `KL begin` record of that dump was lost to a ring-overrun drop, so NAT-089's reader finds no dump with text. What the run did show, by the delivery journal and by a post-hoc reading of the surviving records (outside the pre-registered rows): the whole 2,475,720,704-byte root arrived (179.5 s, 13.79 MB/s, device counters without errors; host 1-minute load average 3.89 at launch), so the NAT-091 shortfall did not recur; the kernel mounted it, init passed 35/35 and df, mount, ps and vm_stat printed (no EIO); and Apple's own `lsd` ran as pid 21 under launchd and printed `denied attempt to escape CPU monitor (missing required entitlement)` about 10 times a second (235 of the 243 timestamped lines in the surviving tail, 234 of them naming lsd[21]; kernel clock 254.1-276.7 s). The flood fills the 32 KiB tail window, so the launchd lines, the `ps -A` lists and every other daemon's output are in the 129,137-byte middle that the dump format does not send. No daemon other than lsd is shown to have run; the ladder rows A1-A7 cannot be evaluated.

acceptance.1_run_and_restore: One run under decision 0036 (commit 0344d11 before the launch): host 1-minute load average 3.89 at launch (no agent build/test/mutation process, checked by ps; another workload's Java process was running at 170-240% CPU of one core); RECOVERY written once, reboot requested 2026-11-12T16:59:23.146Z; the loader appeared +19.4 s; its 360 s deadline returned the phone to Download Mode (`SAMSUNG USB`, +380.4 s on the watcher's clock); NAT-013 restore at 17:05:58Z with the pyusb venv python (bus 5 address 17), Android up 17:06:38Z; check_android outcome pass, assess outcome pass (RECOVERY readback equals the pinned stock, user data directories present). One-shot marker created; no retry.
acceptance.2_analysers: analyze_nat087.py: chain row 9 (chain-verdict-not-pass: PARTIAL because the archive has 2 boots of this image and the collector's manifest says incomplete: 3 capture errors, 2 drops). analyze_nat089.py: row A8 not-evaluated (`no why=2 kernel-log dump with text in the archive`). Both run unchanged after the collector and watcher exited (600 s).
acceptance.3_row_other_than_A1: Recorded as the finding; task NOT completed (a non-pass outcome).

findings: Delivery: 2,475,720,704 of 2,475,720,704 bytes, sha256 equal to the root's (4377e988...62f6), 179.5 s, 13.79 MB/s, 296 chunks, retries 0, device rx_errors/aborts/gaps/rejects/resets 0. NAT-091's 91.82% at 10.10 MB/s did not recur on a host with a 1-minute load average of 3.89 (it was ~30 then): consistent with host load being the cause, not proven.

Log transport: boot 1 = 189 records until +254.85 s (then `unresponsive`, as in earlier runs: the kernel took the USB controller); boot 2 (the loader after its timed return) at +285 s = 517 frames, `KL end why=2 recs=428 bytes=40960`. 83 of the 428 records (7,968 bytes) were lost to 2 producer-reported ring-overrun drops (collector: 205 start failures, 1280 timeouts, 10,716 transfers), among them the `KL begin` record and the first 50 tail records. The same pattern as NAT-088's second boot; NAT-089's reader needs `begin` and therefore yields no dump.

Post-hoc reading (docs/procedures/nat-093/posthoc_boot2.py, written after the result; not a ladder row): the dump length is 170,097 bytes (end of the last record; geometry matches the end line's 428 records), head 8,192 bytes complete (init, the 35 checks, df, mount, ps, vm_stat up to `Pages purged:`), tail range 137,329-170,097 with 345 of 428 records present: 0x21871-0x22b31 and 0x23851-0x244b1 missing.

Apple's lsd ran: the kernel prints `process lsd[21] denied attempt to escape CPU monitor (missing required entitlement).` 234 times in the 22.5 s of surviving tail (kernel clock 254.10-276.66 s), ~10 per second. The message is the printf in osfmk/kern/task_policy.c (apple-xnu reference) that a non-entitled task triggers by asking for a CPU monitor above the global cap (percentage above proc_max_cpumon_percentage, default 50, or an interval above proc_max_cpumon_interval, default 180 s); the kernel clamps the values and goes on, so the message is noise, not a failure, but it is repeated by lsd and fills the log window.

The 8 KiB head ends inside rc's vm_stat output, i.e. before launchd; launchd's own lines, the xpcproxy spawn lines, boot tasks and every other daemon's output are in the 129,137-byte middle of the log (170,097 - 8,192 - 32,768) that the dump does not send. The heartbeat's `ps -A` lists are not in the surviving window either (two memorystatus enter events for pids 26 and 27 at kernel clock 259.31 s and 269.37 s, 10.06 s apart, match the heartbeat's 10 s throttle but are not shown to be it).
In the surviving 25 KiB of tail there is no panic line and no PID 1 exit line (kernel clock up to 276.66 s); that is an absence in a window with holes, not a negative.
established: The whole root was delivered and the kernel booted on it: init 35 checks 0 failed; df/mount/ps/vm_stat printed, no EIO (head text).

An Apple daemon other than launchd (`lsd`, pid 21, name from the kernel's proc name; its plist com.apple.lsd is in the small root and it is not one of the seven self-starting jobs) executed on the S24 under launchd and called into the kernel (the CPU-monitor request). First Apple daemon seen to run on this kernel.
The run happened as described; the phone is back on the stock RECOVERY with Android and user data intact.
not_established: Whether the seven self-starting Apple jobs ran, which other daemons ran or died, whether PID 1 was alive at the end: the launchd lines and the process lists are in the unsent middle or in the lost records.

Why lsd repeats the request ten times a second (a retry loop, a failed XPC lookup, or its normal behaviour under this kernel); that the flood is the only thing hiding the rest (the middle is 129 KB; the flood alone, ~100 B per line at ~10 lines/s, is about 1 KB/s).
That the host load caused the NAT-091 shortfall.
disclosures: The post-hoc reader and the lsd reading were written AFTER the pre-registered analysers returned A8; the verdict rows stay chain 9 / A8. No threshold was changed after the result.

Another workload's Java process (170-240% of one core) and two small services were running on the host during the run; the 1-minute load average was 3.89 at launch and about 4 during the delivery (monitor samples 3.3-4.6).
Decision 0036's idle-host condition (load average below 6, no agent build/test/mutation process) held at launch (3.89; ps checked).
